text:
## Abstract
This query aimed to determine the total number of E. coli sequencing runs available in the European Nucleotide Archive (ENA). We utilized a dedicated federation tool that queries the BRC Analytics ENA endpoint with the NCBI taxonomy identifier for E. coli (taxid 562). The tool returned summary results on sequencing runs, as well as a numeric count representing the total runs matching that taxon. After filtering to limit the retrieval to that taxonomy, the result indicates 551,679 sequencing runs for E. coli at the time of the query. This finding is relevant for large-scale comparative genomics and metagenomics studies involving E. coli, as it highlights the substantial deposit of publicly available sequence data. Monitoring the volume of accessible E. coli data can inform researchers about available resources for addressing questions related to evolution, antimicrobial resistance, and clinical transmission patterns.

## I. Introduction

### Background
Escherichia coli (E. coli) is a widely studied bacterium due to its clinical importance in infections and its utility as a model organism in molecular biology. Public repositories such as the European Nucleotide Archive (ENA) accumulate large sets of sequencing runs, enabling global research on microbial diversity and evolution.

### Literature Review
No literature was retrieved for this query.

### Knowledge Gap
While many E. coli whole-genome sequencing runs have been deposited, an updated snapshot of the total quantity can be valuable for planning large-scale analyses and meta-studies.

### Objective & Hypothesis
• Objective: To identify the number of E. coli sequencing runs currently accessible in ENA.  
• Hypothesis: The repository hosts a large volume of E. coli runs that can enhance comparative genomic analyses.

## II. Materials and Methods

### Study Design
We directly queried the BRC Analytics platform, which proxies the ENA database, for the total count of sequencing runs matching the NCBI taxonomy identifier for E. coli.

### Materials
• Tool Invoked: brc_ena_runs (BRC Analytics’ ENA proxy).  

### Procedures
1. Invoked brc_ena_runs with the following parameters:  
   - taxonomy_id: "562"  
   - limit: 1  
   - offset: 0  

### Statistical Analysis
The returned field “total_in_ena” reported the total number of sequencing runs in ENA for the specified taxonomy. No additional statistical methods were applied.

## III. Results

### Data Presentation
Table 1. Summary of the brc_ena_runs tool output  
| Taxonomy ID | Total Runs | Example Run Accession | Example Study Accession | Instrument Model | Study Title                                      |
|-------------|-----------|------------------------|-------------------------|------------------|--------------------------------------------------|
| 562         | 551,679   | ERR10016945           | PRJEB8667              | HiSeq X Ten      | Pathogenic_lineages_of_enteric_bacteria_in_Nigeria |

### Findings
The tool reported 551,679 sequencing runs for the species E. coli (NCBI taxon 562).

## IV. Discussion

### Interpretation
The large number of E. coli sequencing runs in ENA indicates an extensive resource for microbial genomic research. Researchers can leverage these data to investigate genetic diversity, track antimicrobial resistance mechanisms, and perform multi-locus phylogenetic analyses.

### Context
The result is consistent with the extensive interest in E. coli for both public health and basic research. No direct literature or references beyond the repository data were retrieved for this query.

### Limitations
The reported number reflects the status at the time of this query. ENA data is continuously updated, so future counts may vary. The brc_ena_runs tool provides aggregated results but relies on ENA’s data being accurately curated.

### Conclusion & Future Directions
We observed 551,679 E. coli sequencing runs currently hosted at ENA. Future queries could examine the distribution of these runs by library strategy, geographic regions, or antibiotic resistance traits to inform global epidemiological and evolutionary studies of this key bacterial species.

## References
[1] BRC Analytics ENA Proxy Tool: https://brc-analytics.org/api/v1/ena/taxonomy/562

## Acknowledgments
We acknowledge the BRC Analytics service for providing the ENA proxy tool access to up-to-date sequence records of E. coli.
